title: Data Privacy and Minimization
learningObjectives: Explain the core ideas and terminology of data privacy and minimization.
Recognize the risks or mistakes this topic is intended to prevent.
Apply appropriate defensive practices in a beginner project.
Distinguish this topic from related security concepts and controls.
Review a simple design and justify improvements using evidence.

understand.concept: Privacy-aware design collects only data needed for a defined purpose, explains that purpose, limits retention, protects access, and avoids unnecessary sharing. Data minimization reduces the amount of information that could be exposed or misused. Personal data may include identifiers, location, contact details, or information that can identify someone when combined.
understand.whyItMatters: Collecting less data lowers risk, simplifies protection, and respects user expectations.
understand.analogy: Think of a careful community space where entry, use of shared items, and privacy are guided by clear rules and appropriate checks.
understand.analogyLimit: Software security depends on technical boundaries, data flows, implementation details, and changing threats that this analogy cannot fully represent.

explain.narrative:
Privacy-aware design collects only data needed for a defined purpose, explains that purpose, limits retention, protects access, and avoids unnecessary sharing. Data minimization reduces the amount of information that could be exposed or misused. Personal data may include identifiers, location, contact details, or information that can identify someone when combined.

Apply these principles proportionately. Use established platform and library protections instead of improvising security-critical mechanisms. For a real application, confirm requirements and review the implementation with qualified peers.

examples.title: Collect only needed fields
examples.explanation: The fictional signup only asks for fields needed for its stated function.

examples.title: Set a purpose
examples.code:
const purpose = 'send course progress updates';
console.log(purpose);
examples.explanation: A defined purpose helps justify collection.

examples.title: Avoid unnecessary detail
examples.explanation: A profile need not contain unrelated sensitive details.

examples.title: Plan retention
examples.explanation: Retention should be chosen according to purpose, obligations, and policy—not arbitrary forever storage.

examples.title: Limit exposure in logs
examples.explanation: Event logs can avoid copying personal content.

commonMistakes: Assuming a feature is safe because it works in normal use.
Trusting client-side controls as the only enforcement.
Applying one generic transformation to every kind of input or output.
Exposing credentials or personal data in source, logs, or screenshots.

guidedTask.title: Guided Practice
guidedTask.instructions: Review a fictional registration form with name, phone, address, birth date, hobbies, and email. Identify which fields are necessary for the stated purpose, what should be optional, and how long the data should be kept.
steps: Review a fictional registration form with name, phone, address, birth date, hobbies, and email. Identify which fields are necessary for the stated purpose, what should be optional, and how long the data should be kept.

independentTask.title: Independent Practice
independentTask.instructions: Draft a privacy-minimization plan for a quiz app. List data purpose, essential fields, optional fields, access, retention, deletion, and what should never be logged.
requirements: Use a fictional or toy project and no real secrets or personal data.
Draft a privacy-minimization plan for a quiz app. List data purpose, essential fields, optional fields, access, retention, deletion, and what should never be logged.
Explain the decisions you made and limitations.
Identify at least one test or review step.

hints: Ask why each field is needed.
Consider whether optional data can be omitted.
Avoid collecting sensitive data without a strong purpose.
Limit who can access stored data.
